item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 041703
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Fri Sep 4 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south of the Hawaiian Islands,
and on Hurricane Marie, located several hundred miles west-
southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure may develop well offshore of southwestern
Mexico early next week. Gradual development is possible, and a
tropical depression could form around the middle of next week while
it moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, likely remaining well
offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams/Evans

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...973 MB...28.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 20.4 North, longitude 140.4 West. Karina is moving
toward the west near 10 mph (17 km/h), and it is expected to turn to
the northwest over the weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Gradual weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours,
although Karina is expected to remain a hurricane during the next
day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles
(260 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 973 mb (28.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Future information on Karina can be found under Central Pacific 
basin headers starting with the next advisory at 1100 AM HST, under 
AWIPS header HFOTCPCP5, WMO header WTPA35 PHFO. Products will 
continue to be available on the web at hurricanes.gov. 

Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 33
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Fri Sep 04 2026 
300 
WTPZ41 KNHC 041445
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  33
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 AM HST Fri Sep 04 2026
 
Satellite imagery over the last several hours depicts Karina's 
northwest quadrant degrading as dry air circulates into the system. 
Cloud top temperatures have also warmed slightly, with the deepest 
convection concentrated across Karina's eastern semicircle. The 
latest subjective Dvorak classification from TAFB was 5.0/90 kt, 
with objective ratings from CIMSS between 75-82 kt. Based on 
Karina's degrading structure, the initial intensity was reduced 
slightly to 80 kt.
 
The initial motion was set at 280/9 kt. Karina moved more westward 
than previously anticipated over the last several hours, guided by a 
subtropical ridge to its north. Later today and over the weekend, 
however, Karina is still anticipated to track more northwestward as 
an oncoming upper-level trough pushes the ridge to the east. 
Uncertainty still remains as to how Karina will react to Lowell once 
the two approach each other early next week, but model consensus 
generally exhibits a northwestward motion through the forecast 
period. The official track forecast was shifted leftward slightly in 
light of Karina's more westward initial motion, but after 24 h, 
differences in track from the last advisory were minimal.
 
Gradual weakening is expected to continue as SHIPS guidance
continues to depict Karina in a dry mid-level environment. Vertical
wind shear is expected to increase as well, especially as Karina
makes its more northwestward turn as forecast. The rate of
weakening was once again increased compared to the previous
advisory, and generally falls in line with the model consensus.
Karina is still expected to become post-tropical early next week,
before dissipating thereafter.

Now that Karina is in the Central Pacific, additional information on 
this hurricane can be found under Central Pacific basin headers 
beginning with the next advisory at 1100 AM HST. Future Tropical 
Cyclone Discussions will be issued under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP5 and 
WMO header WTPA45 PHFO. Products will continue to be available on 
the web at hurricanes.gov

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026

...MARIE MOVING WEST-NORTHWESTWARD AWAY FROM LAND...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.1N 117.9W
ABOUT 550 MI...885 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...972 MB...28.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located 
near latitude 20.1 North, longitude 117.9 West. Marie is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and a gradual turn 
toward the northwest is expected within the next day or so.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher 
gusts. A slow weakening trend is expected to begin on Saturday. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles
(295 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 972 mb (28.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of 
the coast of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for 
the next few days and are expected to spread northward to Southern 
California through the weekend. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current 
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026 
167 
WTPZ43 KNHC 041443
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM PDT Fri Sep 04 2026
 
Deep convection is concentrated south and east of a ragged eye, 
while dry air continues to wrap around the northern and western 
portions of the circulation. A recent GPM GMI microwave pass showed 
a slightly elongated eye along with erosion of the western eyewall. 
The latest Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was 5.0/90 kt, while 
remotely-sensed estimates span a broader range of 69-96 kt. The 
initial intensity is maintained at 85 kt for this advisory. 
 
Marie is moving toward the west-northwest around 8 kt, and is 
flanked by a weak mid-level ridge to the west and a strong closed 
low moving into the Pacific Northwest. The hurricane is expected to 
continue on this heading through tonight before the ridge weakens 
and the low digs southeastward over California, causing Marie to 
turn northwestward. Little change has been made to the previous 
forecast through days 3-4. After day 4, the weakening cyclone is 
expected to become increasingly steered by the low- to mid-level 
environmental flow and remain well offshore over the eastern 
Pacific. The official track forecast has been shifted to the right 
of the previous advisory beyond day 4, toward the latest Google 
DeepMind and corrected consensus (HCCA) guidance.

Despite moving over warm waters and through an environment of low 
wind shear, Marie is contending with relatively dry mid-level air, 
which is likely limiting significant strengthening. Similar 
environmental conditions are expected through tonight, supporting 
little change in intensity. Beginning Saturday, Marie is forecast to 
encounter increasingly dry low- and mid-level air along with cooler 
sea surface temperatures, resulting in gradual weakening. More 
substantial weakening is expected next week as the hurricane moves 
into increasingly unfavorable conditions. The official forecast is 
close to the intensity model consensus.
